assumptions.ruleset: Gathering Storm with every expansion and the Leader Pass
assumptions.map: Continents or Pangaea, standard size, 8 civilizations
assumptions.notes: Turn numbers are Standard-speed scaffolding; the site rescales them for other speeds and difficulties. Frederick Barbarossa has one persona and that is the one planned here.

verdict.one_line: Settle wide, give every city a Commercial Hub and a Hansa before it has the population to deserve them, decide by turn 60 whether the extra Military slot buys a city-state and a neighbour or just the escorts, and point the Production at Campuses and a Spaceport.
verdict.why: Free Imperial Cities lets a German city build one district more than its population allows, and the Hansa is the cheapest and best-placed Production district in the game, so a four-population German city can already hold a Commercial Hub, a Hansa and a Campus while a rival city of the same size holds two districts. That is Production and district count, and neither points anywhere by itself; the Production has to be spent on something that ends the game. Science is the default because a Hansa in every city builds Campuses, Universities and the three Spaceport projects faster than any other kit, and nothing in it expires. Domination is the second direction and not Culture because the extra Military policy slot and the +7 against city-states are real from turn one, a weak city-state within reach is a free second city, and the same Hansas then build the siege line. Nothing German makes Great Works or Tourism cheaper.

must_have: Land for seven or more cities, each with a river or flat tiles where a Commercial Hub, a Hansa and an Aqueduct can sit in a cluster.
Hills and resources near the city sites, since the Hansa takes adjacency from every resource and the Mines pay Apprenticeship.
prefer: A city-state within eight tiles of the capital with no Walls by turn 30, for the Domination opening.
Chocolate Hills, Mount Vesuvius or Zhangye Danxia in reach; mineable hills and Great Merchant points feed the Hansa economy.
Hattusa or Johannesburg on the map; strategic resources and Production per improved resource type both multiply through many cities.
map_check.no_go: A small island or a start boxed in to three cities. The extra district and the Hansa are paid per city, and three cities is three Hansas and a kit that has finished growing by turn 80.
map_check.fallback: If the land runs out early, take the Domination direction at turn 60: the nearest city-state falls to four Warriors and two Archers attacking at 27 and 32 with the +7, and a neighbour's cities become German cities with their own extra district the turn they are captured.

kit_levers.name: Holy Roman Emperor
kit_levers.buys: One extra Military policy slot in every government from turn one, and +7 Combat Strength for units attacking city-states.
kit_levers.exploit: The spare Military slot holds Discipline and Agoge at once in the Ancient era, Conscription and Feudal Contract later, so the escorts and the garrison cost nothing in queue time. The +7 turns a weak city-state within eight tiles into a second city at turn 30; take it or send envoys, never both, because the agenda and the grievances make the two routes exclusive.

kit_levers.name: Free Imperial Cities
kit_levers.buys: Every German city can build one specialty district beyond the population limit: two at one population, three at four, four at seven.
kit_levers.exploit: Found a city and queue a Commercial Hub and a Hansa before it has grown at all; rivals wait until four population for their second district. The extra slot is only worth the Production and the citizens to fill it, so the plan grows cities with Aqueducts and Farms as hard as it builds districts, and tracks the district count per city at every checkpoint.

kit_levers.name: Hansa
kit_levers.buys: An Industrial Zone replacement at half cost with +2 adjacency from each adjacent Commercial Hub, +1 from every adjacent resource of any kind and the normal Aqueduct, Dam and Canal bonuses.
kit_levers.exploit: Plan the Commercial Hub and the Hansa together before either is placed: the Hub on the river, the Hansa touching the Hub, the Aqueduct and two or three resource tiles. A +6 Hansa at turn 90 is normal and the Workshop and Factory double it. Craftsmen and Five-Year Plan double the adjacency again, which is where the Spaceport projects come from.

kit_levers.name: U-Boat
kit_levers.buys: A cheaper Submarine with extra sight and a Combat Strength bonus on Ocean tiles, unlocked at Electricity.
kit_levers.exploit: Only the Domination direction on a water map uses it: a pack of six U-Boats clears a rival's navy from the deep water and screens the Battleships that take the coastal capitals. On the Science direction it is a cheap coast guard and nothing more.

kit_levers.name: Iron Crown
kit_levers.buys: Frederick dislikes civilizations that become suzerains of city-states or conquer them.
kit_levers.exploit: Only matters for AI Frederick: keep envoys out of the city-states near him and he stays friendly, which is a free alliance for the Chemistry Eureka on the Science direction.

options.when_it_fits: Seven or more city sites are settled or claimed by turn 60 and no city-state or rival capital is both close and weak. A Commercial Hub, a Hansa and a Campus in every city, Universities in all of them by turn 150, and the Hansa Production spent on Research Labs and the Spaceport out-researches any normal empire; nothing in the kit expires on this path.

A city-state within eight tiles has no Walls at turn 30, or a rival capital is within twelve tiles at turn 50. The +7 takes the city-state with four Warriors and two Archers, the extra Military slot keeps the army cheap, and the Hansas build Trebuchets and Knights for the neighbour by turn 110. The empire that results is the Science empire with three more cities; if the first window is missed the option waits for Bombards.

Two Cultural city-states are met early and the capital lands two Classical wonders off a +4 Hansa. The Production builds Theater Squares and wonders fast, but nothing German makes Great Works, Tourism or Rock Bands cheaper, so take this only when the map has already handed over the pieces and the Science rivals are too far ahead to catch.

direction.commit_test: At turn 100 count the districts: if the three largest cities each hold a Commercial Hub, a Hansa and a Campus with a Library, the direction is Science and it is being spent. If the Hansas exist but the Campuses do not, or the army sits at six Warriors with no city taken, the extra district is being banked and the plan has failed its own test.

checkpoints.test: Era checkpoint. Is the extra district being filled? Every city should hold at least two districts and the three largest at least three with buildings in them; the last four civics should be on the direction's path. Domination: a second city taken since turn 105? Science: Universities in three cities?
checkpoints.pass: Continue; queue Workshops wherever a Hansa lacks one.
checkpoints.fail: Cities with two empty districts and five population are the characteristic failure: stop placing districts there and grow them with Farms, an Aqueduct and a domestic Food route. Civics taken because they were next is the banked-bonus failure; reroute the tree today. Domination with nothing taken since turn 105 has closed until Bombards; switch to Science while the Campus build is cheap.

decision_triggers.name: City-state in reach
decision_triggers.if: At turn 30 a city-state within eight tiles has no Walls and no suzerain with an army nearby.
decision_triggers.then: Take it: four Warriors and two Archers built under Agoge attack at 27 and 32 with the +7, and it is a second city with its own extra district by turn 45. Send no envoys there first; they are lost on the declaration.

decision_triggers.name: Neighbour in Swordsman range
decision_triggers.if: At turn 50 a rival capital is within twelve tiles and has no Walls.
decision_triggers.then: Choose Domination at turn 60. Four Swordsmen, two Archers and a Battering Ram under Oligarchy take it by turn 95; the captured city gets a Commercial Hub and a Hansa like any German city and the empire continues as the Science empire afterward.

decision_triggers.name: Empty districts
decision_triggers.if: At any checkpoint a city holds two or more districts with no building and fewer than six population.
decision_triggers.then: The extra district is being placed and not filled. Stop placing districts in that city, build an Aqueduct and a Farm triangle, run a domestic Food route into it, and resume districts at six population.

decision_triggers.name: Civics drifting
decision_triggers.if: At any era checkpoint the last three civics were not on the chosen direction's path.
decision_triggers.then: The Production is being banked. Re-pick the civic queue today toward the direction's government and policies, and note it as a near-miss on the plan.

decision_triggers.name: Amenities first
decision_triggers.if: Three or more cities show negative Amenities.
decision_triggers.then: Stop settling, build Arenas, buy a luxury, and send envoys to an Industrial or Trade city-state with an Amenity bonus. A wide Germany's limit is happiness, not land.

abort.trigger: Turn 150 with no direction committed: no city taken, no Campus in half the cities, no Theater Square outside the capital, and a civic tree picked in order.
actions: Pick the direction the empire is already closest to; with seven Hansas that is almost always Science. Commit fully; Linear leaders lose by drifting, not by collapsing.
Reroute the civic queue to Recorded History, The Enlightenment and Class Struggle today.
Put a Campus in every city without one before any other district, and a Workshop in every Hansa without one.

fail_state: Turn 200 with eight comfortable cities, a Commercial Hub and a Hansa in every one, Production first in the world and nothing to show for it: no capital taken, Campuses in three cities, no Spaceport site, and half the districts standing empty in six-population cities. Germany has out-built the map and converted none of it, and the extra district has nothing left to add.
common_mistakes: Placing the Hansa before the Commercial Hub. The +2 from the Hub is the biggest single adjacency and the Hub must exist first; a Hansa placed early and alone reads +1 for the rest of the game.
Leaving the second Military slot empty or holding Survey into the Classical era. The slot is the leader ability; Agoge, Conscription and Feudal Contract live in it.
Placing the extra district in a city that cannot staff it. Three districts at four population is allowed, not useful, until the Aqueduct and the Farms arrive.
Sending envoys to the city-state you then attack. Frederick's +7 and his envoys are exclusive; decide at turn 30 and do one.
Treating the Production lead as a score. It builds Campuses and a Spaceport or it builds Bombards; if the queues are wonders and Monuments, it is building nothing.
sources: Civilization VI Civilopedia, Gathering Storm ruleset (Germany, Frederick Barbarossa, Hansa, U-Boat, Free Imperial Cities).
